name: jupiter-rule-check
whatItDecides: Whether a given code-review rule passes or fails against a source file.
currentMechanism: Hardcoded string and regex matching, e.g. code.includes(': any'). One check per rule, no scoring.
callVolume: Once per rule per reviewed file; the demo runs the full rule set on every invocation.
downstreamEffect: A failing rule becomes a critique in the formative-feedback output shown to a developer.
notes: The judgement is about one file in isolation. The incumbent regex is narrow and misses anything phrased differently, but it never produces a false positive on syntax it does not match. Correctness of a replacement can be checked against the source it judges.

name: jupiter-symmetry
whatItDecides: Whether an exchange between two domains is symmetric or asymmetric.
callVolume: Once per candidate domain pair during exploration.
downstreamEffect: Feeds the recommendation and the ranking of suggested exchanges.
notes: The judgement is inherently about a RELATION between two domains, not a property of one state. Flagged in advance as the shape that failed in GRAPH_EDGES.

name: jupiter-impedance-severity
whatItDecides: How severe the impedance is between two domains: low, medium, or high.
currentMechanism: A lookup table plus if/else inference.
callVolume: Once per domain pair, several impedances per pair.
downstreamEffect: Severity gates whether an exchange is recommended at all.
notes: Ordinal output with named levels, which suits a score question — but the thing being scored is again a relation between two domains.

name: jupiter-recommendation
whatItDecides: Whether to implement, research further, or not recommend an exchange.
downstreamEffect: The headline output of the discovery engine; determines what a user is told to do.
notes: A closed three-option answer space, which fits choice well. But the inputs are the outputs of assessSymmetry and assessSeverity, so its quality is capped by theirs.

name: jupiter-pattern-match
whatItDecides: Whether a candidate pattern counts as a match for a given structure.
currentMechanism: Fingerprint hashing plus a similarity score filtered by a hardcoded threshold.
callVolume: Every candidate pattern against every query structure; the highest-volume site in the repo.
downstreamEffect: Determines the candidate set everything downstream ranks.
notes: A replacement can be checked against the structures it compares. Highest call volume of the eight sites, so latency and cost matter most here.

name: jupiter-priority-order
whatItDecides: The order in which feedback items are presented to a developer.
currentMechanism: A fixed priority array: security > architecture > performance > style > tests.
downstreamEffect: Presentation order only; no gating, nothing is dropped.
notes: Ordering is comparative by construction. The fixed array is defensible and rarely wrong, so the incumbent is strong and the payoff is cosmetic.

name: jupiter-approval-ready
whatItDecides: Whether a reviewed change is ready for approval.
currentMechanism: A single rule: zero actionable critiques.
downstreamEffect: Gates approval, so a wrong answer either blocks good work or waves through bad work.
notes: Binary output, checkable against the critique list it reads. The incumbent rule is crude but fully predictable.

name: jupiter-rank-suggestions
currentMechanism: Weighted score adjustments with hardcoded constants of +0.2, +0.1 and -0.3.
callVolume: Once per exploration run, over all suggestions.
downstreamEffect: Ordering of results presented to a user.
notes: Ranking requires comparing items to each other, which no single-state call can do. Per-item scoring followed by sorting in code is the only viable shape.

name: context-triage-keep-drop
whatItDecides: Whether a tool output is kept verbatim, dropped, or escalated to a text model.
currentMechanism: Eight literal questions recombined by a hand-set weighted score, with supersession computed deterministically in code.
callVolume: Once per tool output; 151 in the current session.
downstreamEffect: Nothing is deleted — it produces a manifest. Applying it would be a separate reversible step.
notes: CALIBRATION ANCHOR, KNOWN GOOD. Already measured across three iterations. Literal questions reached the ends on 53 to 83 percent of items. A scorer that rates this low is miscalibrated.

name: graph-edge-typing
whatItDecides: What relationship one item has to another, and whether that relationship is directional.
currentMechanism: Nothing yet — a drafted question set, never shipped.
downstreamEffect: Would build a knowledge graph from documents.
notes: CALIBRATION ANCHOR, KNOWN BAD. Measured on 16 real pairs: directional reached the ends on 0 percent, statedNotInferred on 6 percent, relationship only 38 percent. A scorer that rates this highly is miscalibrated.

name: duplicate-read-dedup
whatItDecides: Whether a tool output is a repeat of one already seen, so only one copy is kept.
currentMechanism: Hashing the first 200 characters and grouping.
callVolume: Every tool output; 544 in local history.
downstreamEffect: Would reclaim roughly 21,941 tokens, 97 percent of it duplicate file reads.
notes: CONTROL, SHOULD SCORE LOW ON FIT. The deterministic hash already solves it completely and exactly. A model adds cost and uncertainty to a solved problem. Included to check the scorer does not reward payoff while ignoring that no judgement is required.

name: doc-chunk-relevance
whatItDecides: Whether a retrieved documentation chunk should enter a prompt.
currentMechanism: Nothing — retrieved chunks currently all enter the prompt.
callVolume: Once per chunk per retrieval; unbounded in principle.
downstreamEffect: Controls what context a coding model reads, so a wrong discard silently degrades an answer.
notes: Validated on 18 real doc chunks: three questions JEV-SAFE, two MARGINAL, no failures. answersTheQuestion reached the ends on 100 percent. Blocked in practice because the context7 server on this machine points at a package that does not exist.

name: course-section-qa
whatItDecides: Whether a generated teaching section ships, needs revision, or should be regenerated.
currentMechanism: Nothing — no generated-content quality gate exists anywhere on this machine.
notes: Validated on 16 real prose sections: three JEV-SAFE, one MARGINAL, no failures. No HTML course pipeline exists yet, so this would be built rather than retrofitted.

name: tool-call-gate
whatItDecides: Whether a tool call is auto-approved, prompted for, or refused.
currentMechanism: Static permission rules in settings.json: allow lists and prefix wildcards.
callVolume: Every tool call; 544 in local history, 381 of them Bash.
downstreamEffect: A wrong auto-approval runs something destructive without asking. A wrong prompt is merely friction.
notes: Drafted, never validated. The field reports one measured instance: 41 percent fewer prompts over 1,013 real calls with zero unsafe auto-approvals out of 94. Errors are maximally asymmetric here.
